tools.name: ailang_builtins
tools.description:
List AILANG builtin functions with documentation, grouped by module.
`search` filters lines case-insensitively; empty returns everything.

tools.name: ailang_check
tools.description:
Type-check AILANG source. `code` is a whole module; the module line may be
omitted or be `module main`. Returns the ai-check JSON report on stdout:
check.passed and check.errors (with locations and fixes), and verify: each
function's requires/ensures proved with Z3 (verify.results: verified,
counter

tools.name: ailang_eval
tools.description:
Evaluate one pure AILANG expression and print it with show(). Builtins are
in scope; for stdlib functions (map, filter, ...) use ailang_run with
explicit imports.

tools.name: ailang_prompt
tools.description:
Call this FIRST: the AILANG teaching prompt (syntax rules, templates,
stdlib map). AILANG is not in your training data the way Python is; code
written without this prompt rarely type-checks.

tools.name: ailang_run
tools.description:
Run AILANG source in the hosted sandbox. Entry point is `main`, with no
arguments. Only the IO capability is granted (println works; FS, Net,
Process, Env and AI are refused by name before the program starts), and the
run is killed at the policy timeout. stdout is the program's output; stderr
carrie

tools.name: ailang_versions
tools.description: List all AILANG versions the server can answer for.

tools.name: benchmark_run
tools.description: One run's full result (code, compile_ok, runtime_ok, stdout_ok, cost, tokens).

tools.name: benchmarks_compare
tools.description:
Pairwise model comparison.
Output: {a_only_passes, b_only_passes, both, neither}

tools.name: benchmarks_for_model
tools.description:
Where does a given model pass/fail? Optional version filter.
Output: {passes: [...], fails_by_category: {...}, total_cost}

tools.name: benchmarks_list
tools.description: List benchmark suites and runs, optionally filtered to a since_version cutoff.

tools.name: changelog_for_version
tools.description: What changed in a given release (added/changed/fixed/breaking).

tools.name: design_doc
tools.description: Full design doc by slug (e.g. "m-agent-mcp-website").

tools.name: design_docs_list
tools.description:
List planned/implemented/rejected design docs, optionally filtered by version.
state = "planned" | "implemented" | "rejected" | ""; empty = all.

tools.name: docs_nav
tools.description:
The AILANG docs site's navigation tree for a version, as JSON: section and
page titles with their paths.

tools.name: docs_search
tools.description:
Full-text search of the AILANG documentation for a version (case-insensitive,
on page titles and text). Returns the top 10 matches, docs pages before
archived teaching prompts, each with its path, title, first 10 headings and
an excerpt around the match.

tools.name: effects_catalog
tools.description: All declared effects with capability mapping and the version they appeared in.

tools.name: example_for_concept
tools.description:
Best-fit examples for a free-form concept query ("how do I use effects?").
Filters server-side on why + title; returns up to 5 matches.

tools.name: example_get
tools.description: Full source + metadata for one example by path.

tools.name: examples_list
tools.description:
Filter examples that pass under for_version, optionally by features/status.
features = comma-separated tags ("effects,records"); empty = no filter.
status = "passing" | "failing" | ""; empty = passing only.

tools.name: executor_whoami
tools.description:
Which account this connection is signed in as (its user ID) and which app
connected it (for example claude.ai or chatgpt.com).

tools.name: install_guide
tools.description:
Harness-aware install instructions for AILANG.
harness: "claude-code" | "gemini-cli" | "codex-cli" | "manual" | "build-from-source" | ""
platform: only meaningful for "manual" (e.g. "darwin-arm64", "linux-amd64"); ignored otherwise
Empty harness returns ALL harnesses + the remote_mcp config block.

tools.name: limitations_list
tools.description: Known limitations (Y-combinator, etc.) optionally filtered by category.

tools.name: onboarding_guide
tools.description:
Step-by-step guide to getting started with AILANG, for an AI coding agent
and for a human developer. role: "agent" | "developer" | "" (both). The
guide for both roles is returned whatever role says; pick the part you need.

tools.name: prompt_get
tools.description:
Fetch the canonical teaching prompt for a version.
kind = "agent" | "devtools" | "compact" (full prompt = empty).

tools.name: roadmap
tools.description: What's shipping next, what's been rejected and why.

tools.name: stdlib_module
tools.description: Full module: exports + signatures + docstrings.

tools.name: stdlib_modules
tools.description: List stdlib modules available in this AILANG version with one-line summaries.

tools.name: stdlib_search
tools.description:
Find stdlib functions by name, signature, or keyword.
Filters the pre-built search index server-side; returns top 20 matches.

tools.name: submit_feedback
tools.description: Send a bug report, feature request, documentation gap or limitation about AILANG to the AILANG team. Use it only when the user asks to report something, and leave out personal or confidential information. Categories: bug, feature, docs, limitation. Body up to 10 KB, snippet up to 4 KB. `contact` is

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "ailang_check" is 640 chars, far longer than this server's median (122). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.
